title: KV-cache dtype sweep of the context edition on one physical RTX 5090
question: docs/29 F5 records the KV-dtype lever as unmeasured: the pinned r34 build advertises seventeen --kv-cache-dtype values, every number this project publishes used fp8, and no 4-bit scheme had ever been measured here for capacity, retrieval or fidelity. A reader in the release megathread asked directly whether quantized KV destroys long-context quality. This receipt answers both.
claim_scope: One physical NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 on the user's own AIBoss host, 32,607 MiB, driver 610.57.04, on the promoted four-module release image. Every arm serves the same context-edition checkpoint at the same qualified profile; --kv-cache-dtype is the only deliberate variable, and --max-model-len moves only for the one arm that cannot hold the native window. Nothing here was measured on the rental RTX PRO 6000 and no number here may be differenced against one.
one_variable_caveat: The KV dtype is the only flag changed, but it is not the only thing that changes. The engine derives the attention backend and the attention block size from the KV dtype, so each arm is measured as the engine actually serves it: fp8 runs on FLASHINFER at block 1600, bfloat16 on FLASH_ATTN at block 800, and the whole per-token-head family on TRITON_ATTN at block 1584 or 3104 because TRITON_ATTN is the only backend that accepts them. Capacity and speed differences below are therefore dtype-plus-backend effects and are labelled as such wherever the backend is the cause.

verdict.headline: fp8 is confirmed as the right default for the context edition's native-window profile, and the alternatives are now measured rather than assumed.
verdict.does_any_arm_beat_fp8_on_the_frontier: No. The frontier is native-or-beyond context on 32 GB with retrieval intact, and fp8 already sits on it at 265,122 allocated tokens with 5/5 needles exact at 261,795. Two arms dominate fp8 on capacity and on fidelity simultaneously -- int8_per_token_head and fp8_per_token_head both allocate 272,453 tokens (1.04x against fp8's 1.01x) and both sit closer to the bfloat16-KV reference than fp8 does -- but both pay 3.0x prefill at the native window, 544.3 s and 546.8 s against 180.4 s for the same 261,795-token prompt. On a native-context serving profile prefill is the user-visible cost, so a three-minute prompt becoming a nine-minute prompt is not a trade this profile takes for 7,331 tokens of capacity and a fidelity gain that no retrieval or capability gate can see.
verdict.what_the_alternatives_are_good_for: int4_per_token_head is the real capacity lever and it belongs to the small classes, not to this one: 502,667 allocated tokens at the native window, 1.92x concurrency, and 5/5 plus 5/5 needles exact at 261,795 and 98,313 tokens. Its cost is fidelity -- 0.005948 nats of mean truncated KL against the bfloat16 reference, 3.6x fp8's 0.001655 -- and 2.78x prefill.
verdict.answer_to_the_readers_question: Quantized KV does not destroy long-context quality on this model, and the shipped fp8 default is not the weak link. Against a bfloat16 KV cache at a 98,304-token context, fp8 keeps 95.60 % top-1 agreement with a mean truncated KL of 0.001655 nats, and every arm including 4-bit retrieved every needle exactly at every depth tested. But retrieval is not fidelity: int4_per_token_head passes 10/10 needles while carrying 3.6x fp8's distributional error, so a needle table alone would have called 4-bit free when it is not.
verdict.confounder_stated_plainly: The capacity advantage of the per-token-head family is not a KV-byte effect and must not be read as one. Those arms cost MORE per token than fp8, 35,360 against 34,816 B/token. Their extra 7,331 tokens come from a CUDA-graph pool of 0.06 GiB against fp8's 0.45 GiB, which is a property of TRITON_ATTN, and it lifts the KV pool from 9.28 to 9.67 GiB.

runtime_image.modules_note: the first three digests are byte-identical to identity.patch_files_sha256 in receipts/qualification-5090-context.json, so this sweep's baseline arm is comparable with the published qualification. They are baked into the image here rather than bind-mounted.

profile_held_fixed.the_only_variable: --kv-cache-dtype, and --max-model-len only where an arm refuses the native window

what_this_measurement_is_not.not_the_v5_kld_protocol: The fidelity numbers here are NOT KLD on the v5 fidelity suite and must never be differenced against 0.002699883159684943, 0.003409, 0.010604 or any other published KLD figure. Those are full-distribution divergences over millions of scored positions against a BF16 weight reference. These are truncated top-20 divergences over at most 173 paired positions against a bfloat16 KV-cache reference, measuring a different quantity of a different component of the system.
what_this_measurement_is_not.not_a_capability_claim: No downstream capability suite, no image gate, no tool-calling gate and no repetition or non-termination check was run on any arm. The only behavioural gates here are needle retrieval and greedy continuation agreement.
what_this_measurement_is_not.not_a_serving_qualification: This is not a rank-1 qualification of any non-fp8 arm. Gate 3 (combined long text plus a 7 MP image) and gate 4 (the image suite) were not run for any arm, so no arm other than fp8 has been shown to serve the multimodal profile at all.
what_this_measurement_is_not.no_concurrency: Every arm ran at --max-num-seqs 1. The concurrency figures quoted are the engine's own maximum-concurrency line, not measured concurrent serving.

resolution_of_the_fidelity_measurement.protocol: Four deterministic prompts built from the same held-out literary corpus, sized by the server's own tokenizer to 98,266-98,344 tokens, byte-identical across arms and verified by sha256. Each is completed greedily for 64 tokens at temperature 0 with top-20 logprobs at every generated position.
resolution_of_the_fidelity_measurement.pairing_rule: A position is paired only while both arms conditioned on an identical token prefix. The first divergent position is itself paired -- its conditioning prefix is still identical -- and everything after it is discarded. That gives 70 to 173 paired positions per arm pair, and the count is reported with every figure because it is not constant.
resolution_of_the_fidelity_measurement.top1_agreement: fraction of paired positions where the two arms' argmax token is the same.
resolution_of_the_fidelity_measurement.truncated_kl: KL(base || arm) restricted to the base arm's top-20 support, both sides renormalised over those 20 tokens. Where a base token is absent from the arm's top-20 its logprob is floored at the arm's 20th, which over-estimates that token's probability and therefore UNDER-estimates the divergence: every KL here is a lower bound. The rate at which that floor is used is reported as support_miss_rate and runs 1.10 % to 4.36 %.
resolution_of_the_fidelity_measurement.delta_logprob: mean and max absolute difference in the log-probability the two arms assign to the base arm's argmax token, over paired positions where that token appears in both top-20 lists. This one is free of the truncation caveat.
resolution_of_the_fidelity_measurement.run_to_run_control: Every arm re-ran prompt 0 in the same server process. All four arms returned byte-identical text, identical token ids and a maximum absolute logprob difference of exactly 0.0, so this harness has no run-to-run noise at all and every cross-arm difference reported is the dtype and its backend.
resolution_of_the_fidelity_measurement.what_would_sharpen_it: More prompts, longer generations, and full-vocabulary rather than top-20 logprobs. Four prompts at 64 tokens is enough to rank the arms by an order of magnitude, and is not enough to put a confidence interval on any single arm's KL.

nvfp4_specifically.why_it_is_here: Added to this receipt at Main's request during the run, on the owner's report that the vLLM-GG fork serves GLM-5.2 with an nvfp4 KV cache. That precedent claim is the owner's and is UNVERIFIED BY US: no GLM-5.2 run, no GLM configuration and no GLM log was inspected for this receipt.
nvfp4_specifically.cost_to_answer: Zero extra GPU time. nvfp4 and nvfp4_ds_mla were already in the seventeen-dtype startup census, and the backend probe is CPU-only.
nvfp4_specifically.result: Neither starts. Both fail identically and early, in attention-backend selection, before any KV cache is sized and before the GDN hybrid coordinator is reached.
nvfp4_specifically.what_the_engine_names_as_missing: Not head_size 256, not sm120, not the Gated DeltaNet hybrid, and not the exl3 weight path. All five candidate backends reject on the KV dtype alone: FLASH_ATTN, FLASHINFER, TRITON_ATTN, FLEX_ATTENTION and TURBOQUANT each report exactly 'kv_cache_dtype not supported'.
nvfp4_specifically.does_the_mla_path_rescue_it: No, at least not by shape. Replaying the build's own CudaPlatform.get_valid_backends off-GPU finds no valid backend for nvfp4 or nvfp4_ds_mla in any of the four shapes probed, including use_mla=True at head_size 576, where TRITON_MLA and the FlashInfer MLA backends also answer 'kv_cache_dtype not supported'. See attention_backend_probe for the full matrix and its own caveats.
nvfp4_specifically.probe_caveat: The off-GPU probe is validated against reality: it reproduces the observed backend choice for every dtype that actually started (FLASHINFER for fp8, FLASH_ATTN for bfloat16 and auto, TRITON_ATTN for the three per-token-head schemes, and TURBOQUANT accepting the four turboquant presets at selection time). Where a cell reports an AssertionError the backend's validator reached for a global vLLM config that a bare probe does not have; those cells are inconclusive, not negative, and they are all MLA cells.
nvfp4_specifically.what_a_follow_up_build_task_needs: An attention backend on this fork that advertises nvfp4 for a non-MLA decoder. Until one exists, nvfp4 KV is unreachable for Qwen3.8-27B regardless of what the flag list accepts, and --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 is a startup failure rather than a slow or inaccurate configuration.

turboquant_specifically.result: All four presets -- turboquant_k8v4, turboquant_4bit_nc, turboquant_k3v4_nc, turboquant_3bit_nc -- load the model successfully and then fail during KV cache creation.
turboquant_specifically.verbatim: ValueError: Unknown TurboQuant cache dtype: 'auto'. Valid presets: turboquant_k8v4, turboquant_4bit_nc, turboquant_k3v4_nc, turboquant_3bit_nc
turboquant_specifically.mechanism: The TURBOQUANT backend accepts these dtypes at selection time -- the off-GPU probe confirms it -- so the failure is downstream, in vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py where the per-layer cache_dtype_str is computed as `"auto" if kv_cache_spec.kv_quant_mode == KVQuantMode.NONE else self.cache_config.cache_dtype`. The TurboQuant presets are not mapped into KVQuantMode, so the spec reports NONE, the string 'auto' is forwarded to the backend, and TurboQuantConfig.from_cache_dtype('auto') raises. Two halves of the build disagree about whether these dtypes are quantized.
turboquant_specifically.consequence: The whole TurboQuant family is unreachable on this model in this build, which retires the docs/29 F5 plan item that named turboquant_4bit_nc as a sweep arm. It is a build defect and not a hardware or model limit; a KVQuantMode mapping for the four presets is the whole fix.
turboquant_specifically.not_claimed: We did not patch it, and we therefore do not know whether TurboQuant would work, be fast, or be accurate on this model if the mapping existed.

structural_findings_about_the_kv_law.charged_layers_are_an_integer_and_the_re: The exact law is needed(L) = ceil(L/B)*B*a + M with a = k * (bytes per token per full-attention layer). Two refusals per configuration determine k to within 0.03 of an integer in all ten cases, and k is 17 with MTP-3 and 16 with MTP off, for every dtype. The model has 16 full-attention layers; the seventeenth is the engine's own 'Add 3 padding layers, may waste at most 6.25 % KV cache memory' allowance, which is exactly one sixteenth.
structural_findings_about_the_kv_law.this_reproduces_the_published_fp8_law_ex: fp8 under MTP-3 comes out at a = 34,816 B/token and M = 0.63 GiB in the published form, digit for digit the docs/34 s10.2 figures, from an independent set of refusals on a different image four months of receipts later. That is the control that licenses reading the other four dtypes off the same procedure.
structural_findings_about_the_kv_law.one_correction_offered_not_taken: Under MTP off the exact form gives a = 32,768 B/token exactly -- k = 16 with no padding sixteenth -- against the published 32,932. The published figure was fitted with the unquantized divisor and carries a worst-case +/- 82 B/token; docs/34 already noted it as '1.005 x the fp8 floor', and the exact form says the 0.5 % was rounding and it IS the floor. This is offered as a sharpening, not applied: it moves an fp8 baseline that four documents cite, it is measured here at utilisation 0.72 on a 5090 rather than on the 24 GiB proxy the published figure came from, and it changes no published class length.
structural_findings_about_the_kv_law.M_is_essentially_dtype_independent: The fixed per-request term sits at 0.619 to 0.631 GiB under MTP-3 and 0.140 to 0.148 GiB with MTP off, across a 3.9x range of per-token cost from 17,952 to 69,632 B/token. It does not shrink when the KV cache does, which is what one expects if it is dominated by Gated DeltaNet recurrent state and draft bookkeeping rather than by attention KV -- and it is the reason no KV dtype rescues the withdrawn 16 GB MTP-3 row.
structural_findings_about_the_kv_law.four_bit_is_not_half: int4_per_token_head costs 17,952 B/token against fp8's 34,816, which is 51.6 % and not 50 %. The last dimension halves as expected, and then the dynamic per-token-head scales add 32 B per token per layer -- two float32 values per KV head -- which is 3.1 % back.

class_consequence_summary.rule: memory form of the >=15 % headroom rule, a*L + M <= pool/1.15, L a multiple of 4096. The token form is not equivalent and over-publishes once M is nonzero.
class_consequence_summary.pools_are_held_not_remeasured: The class pools are the fp8-derived figures from docs/34 and receipts/qualification-24gib-capped.json. Only a and M vary by dtype here. On the 5090 the KV pool did move with dtype, 9.28 GiB for fp8 against 9.67 GiB for every other arm, so a class-accurate answer would re-measure the pool on a ballasted proxy per dtype. That is not done here and every class number below is therefore a prediction, marked as one.
class_consequence_summary.arithmetic_is_controlled: Feeding the published fp8 law into this same function reproduces 24,576 at 25.4 % headroom and 28,672 at 27.3 % headroom, the two published figures, exactly.
class_consequence_summary.which_arms_would_change_the_published_fi: One. int4_per_token_head roughly doubles both: the 24 GiB MTP-3 row goes 24,576 -> 53,248 (requirement 1.5556 GiB, 15.1 % headroom, on the edge of the rule) and the 16 GiB MTP-off row goes 28,672 -> 57,344 (1.0912 GiB, 18.9 %). int8_per_token_head and fp8_per_token_head change neither -- both land on the same 24,576 and 28,672 with slightly thinner headroom, 24.1 % and 20.9 %, because they cost marginally more per token than fp8. bfloat16 halves both, to 12,288 and 12,288.
class_consequence_summary.the_16_gb_mtp_3_row_stays_withdrawn_for_: Its pool is 0.553 GiB, the rule allows 0.4809 GiB, and the smallest fixed term any dtype achieves is 0.6188 GiB. Even a free KV cache would not start it. This closes the question of whether a cheaper KV dtype rescues that row: it does not, because the term that blocks it is not KV.
class_consequence_summary.these_are_predictions_not_starts: No 24 GiB or 16 GiB proxy was run in this sweep. Every window in class_consequence is arithmetic on a measured law and a held pool, and none of them has been started.
